task.description:
WF-03 Step 2 gate -- validate CODE-DESIGNER's design for ISS-0426 (lib/letflow/design/iss426-wallclock-test-contention.md). You are a HARD GATE: PASS or FAIL, and a FAIL routes back to CODE-DESIGNER for rework. Apply your own role's standard checks (every acceptance criterion covered, no implementation code, unambiguous enough to build from). This description names the run-specific points that most need your scrutiny -- it does not replace your checklist.

SCRUTINISE THESE SPECIFICALLY:

1. THE TEST-ONLY SEAM ON PRODUCTION CODE. The design adds a new `@doc false` test-only synchronous entry point to Letflow.Engine.Lua.Executor so Group 1 tests can call the private run_script/3 without going through Task.Supervisor.async_nolink/Task.yield. Adding production surface area purely to serve tests is a real design smell and needs to clear a bar. CODE-DESIGNER cites this file's OWN existing precedent: build_script_error/3 at executor.ex:449, a public-with-@doc-false function whose comment at line 438 justifies it via REQ-162 design section 4.2/AC3. ORCH has confirmed that precedent exists. YOUR job is to judge whether it genuinely LICENSES this new seam or is being stretched: read executor.ex:438-455 and REQ-162's design, and decide whether the new seam is the same KIND of thing. Consider explicitly whether a test-support module, a @compile-guarded definition, or simply making run_script/3 public-with-@doc-false would be cleaner, and whether the design's answer is reasoned or merely asserted.
   CRITICAL SUB-CHECK: does the seam BYPASS the wall-clock kill for the paths under test? If Group 1 tests no longer exercise the Task/timeout wrapper at all, confirm the design states what is thereby NO LONGER covered by those tests, and that something else still covers the wrapper. A restructure that silently deletes coverage of REQ-155's LUA-10 layer-2 kill would be a worse defect than the flake it fixes. ISS-0426's own scope note warns that option (b) 'moves the threshold without removing the sensitivity' -- the mirror-image risk here is removing the sensitivity by removing the test.

2. OPEN QUESTIONS LEFT TO ELIXIR-DEV. The design closes with OQ-1 (exact seam signature) and OQ-2 (whether the 2 max_heap_words-limited Group 1 sites need a different mechanism, since they route through run_with_heap_limit/5 rather than run_script/3). Your role's bar is 'unambiguous enough to build from'. Judge whether these are legitimate implementation latitude or whether OQ-2 in particular is an unresolved DESIGN question being passed downstream -- if the design does not know whether its own mechanism covers 2 of its 11 Group 1 sites, that is a design gap, not a build detail. Say which it is and FAIL if it is the latter.

3. THE ENUMERATION'S CORRECTNESS. CODE-DESIGNER reports finding ISSUE-FIXER's enumeration incomplete: 5 additional Group-1-shaped call sites in the REQ-154 instruction-budget block, and 2 tests (executor_test.exs:656 and :887) that are internally MIXED (one Group-1-shaped call and one genuinely-racing Group-2 call in the same test body). ISS-0426's acceptance criterion 1 requires the enumeration be explicit and complete, with each test's timing assumption stated. VERIFY THE ENUMERATION YOURSELF against test/letflow/engine/lua/executor_test.exs -- do not accept either agent's count. Report the count you independently derive. The mixed tests are the highest-risk item: confirm the design says exactly what happens to a test whose two halves need opposite treatments, and that the answer does not lose either half's coverage.

4. TAG WIRING (ISS-0426 AC5). The design adds @tag :lua_wallclock_race, excluded in test/test_helper.exs and run in a new isolated subprocess in lib/mix/tasks/letflow.check.test.ex (a sibling to run_wasm_hang_tests/0). Verify the wiring genuinely mirrors the :wasm_hang shape in BOTH files and that a plain `mix test` and CI both stay correct. Check the deliberate choice NOT to reuse the :wasm_hang tag is sound (CODE-DESIGNER's stated reason: same family, different root cause). Confirm CI actually invokes mix letflow.check.test -- read .github/workflows/ci.yml -- because if CI runs plain `mix test` instead, the newly tagged Group 2 tests would be SILENTLY EXCLUDED FROM CI ENTIRELY and never run anywhere. That would be a BLOCKER.

5. HARD CONSTRAINT AC4. Confirm the design changes NO production timeout semantics: config/config.exs:17's 5_000 untouched, no production timeout constant raised or removed. This is REQ-155's LUA-10 security control.

6. CONCURRENT-RUN CONTENTION. lib/mix/tasks/letflow.check.test.ex is also owned by the live run WF03-ISS0418-20260902. Verify the design's change there is genuinely minimal and additive as claimed (one new sibling function, one new call site, zero existing lines touched) -- a claim ORCH will rely on when sequencing the merge. If it is not, say so, because ORCH's merge plan depends on it.

You may READ any file. Do not edit lib/ or test/ -- your step writes only its own handoff (and you may amend the design ONLY if your role's instructions permit it; otherwise FAIL back to CODE-DESIGNER). Complete the handoff with a clear PASS/FAIL, your independently derived enumeration count, and per-point verdicts. Commit it to branch feature/WF03-ISS0426-20260902.
